q1: The shaft speed of a servo axis, reconstructed from the encoder angle.
q2: I measure the shaft angle with a 20-bit encoder and the commanded motor torque is known; the model is in the attached file. The loop samples every 0.5 ms. Encoder error is hard-limited to 23 µrad in magnitude, with a standard deviation of 13.3 urad. The unmodelled disturbance acceleration never exceeds 1.31 rad/s^2; treated as a random sequence that is white and constant over each sample, its standard deviation is 0.756 rad/s². At start-up the angle is known to within 3.18 mrad worst case (standard deviation 1.84 mrad) and the speed to within 2.64 rad/s worst case (standard deviation 1.52 rad/s). These errors are bounded and uniform-like rather than Gaussian, so only their means and variances should be relied on.
q3: I want the speed estimate with the lowest achievable mean-square error. Only the settled behaviour is of interest, so a fixed-gain estimator is acceptable.

q1: Mass velocity of a mass-spring-damper stage; only position is sensed.
q2: Position sensor on the mass, actuator force known, model attached. Sample period is 500 µs. The position reading is wrong by at most 45 um, as a hard limit. Unmodelled acceleration acting on the mass is bounded in magnitude by 0.111 m/s^2. The mass velocity cannot exceed 0.701 m/s in magnitude during operation; a hardware limiter enforces that.
q3: A guaranteed error limit: the velocity estimate must stay within 28.9 mm/s of the true value for every noise and disturbance realisation consistent with the bounds above, not just on average.

q1: Shaft speed on a servo axis.
q2: Encoder angle is the only measurement; motor torque is the known input and the plant model is attached. Sampling rate is 0.5 kHz. The encoder error has a per-sample variance of 6.52864e-9 rad^2 and can never be larger than 140 urad. The disturbance acceleration is limited to 1.5 rad/s^2 in absolute value; statistically it is a white sequence, piecewise constant over a sample, with standard deviation 0.866 rad/s^2. Initial angle error is at most 16.7 mrad with standard deviation 9.64 mrad, and initial speed error is at most 644 mrad/s with standard deviation 0.372 rad/s. None of this is Gaussian; the distributions are bounded and I can only vouch for means and variances.
q3: The requirement is on average accuracy: the mean-square error of the speed estimate must not exceed 8.87364e-5 (rad/s)^2. It is a steady-state requirement, so a constant-gain solution is fine.
